'''Michael T. McManus''' is an American professor of Microbiology and Immunology at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF), where he holds the Vincent and Stella Coates Endowed Chair. He directs the Keck Center for Noncoding RNAs and the UCSF ViraCore facility. His research areas include RNA biology, gene regulation, immunology, and [[high-throughput screening]]. McManus serves as an Investigator at the [[Chan Zuckerberg Biohub]].<ref name="Bashyam2008">{{cite journal |last1=Bashyam |first1=Hema |title=Michael T. McManus: Interrupting biology |journal=Journal of Experimental Medicine |volume=205 |issue=3 |pages=506–507 |date=2008 |doi=10.1084/jem.2053pi |pmid=18347104 |pmc=2275373}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Michael T. McManus earned his Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Horticultural Science from Auburn University in 1991. He completed his Ph.D. in Biochemistry and [[Molecular genetics|Molecular Genetics]] at the University of Alabama at Birmingham in 2000, under the mentorship of Dr. Stephen L. Hajduk. His doctoral research involved identifying mitochondrial [[RNA editing]] ligases from ''Trypanosoma brucei'', providing support for an enzymatic model for insertional/deletional RNA editing.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=McManus |first1=MT |last2=Shimamura |first2=M |last3=Grams |first3=J |last4=Hajduk |first4=SL |title=Identification of candidate mitochondrial RNA editing ligases from Trypanosoma brucei |journal=RNA |volume=7 |issue=2 |pages=167–175 |year=2001 |doi=10.1017/s1355838201002072 |pmid=11233974 |pmc=1370075}}</ref>

He then conducted postdoctoral research in mammalian [[RNA interference]] (RNAi) and [[microRNA]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) under Nobel Laureate [[Phillip A. Sharp]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=McManus

== Career ==
McManus began started as an assistant professor at UCSF in the Department of Microbiology and Immunology and the UCSF Diabetes Center. He became a full professor in 2016, holding the Vincent and Stella Coates Endowed Chair<ref name="UCSFProfile">{{Cite web 
|title=Michael T. McManus, PhD - UCSF Profiles 
|url=https://profiles.ucsf.edu/michael.mcmanus 
|website=UCSF Profiles 
|access-date=March 30, 2025
}}</ref>

He is the director of the Keck Center for Noncoding RNAs and the core director of the UCSF ViraCore facility. Since 2022, Dr. McManus has served as an investigator at the [[Chan Zuckerberg Biohub]].<ref name="CZBiohubInvestigators">{{Cite web 
|title=Investigators - Chan Zuckerberg Biohub 
|url=https://www.czbiohub.org/sf/people/#investigators 
|website=Chan Zuckerberg Biohub 
|access-date=March 30, 2025
}}</ref> He is also a member of the [[UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center]] and has held memberships at the [[Innovative Genomics Institute]]<ref name="IGIFunding2025">{{Cite web 
|title=IGI Funds 24 New Research Projects 
|url=https://innovativegenomics.org/news/igi-funds-24-new-research-projects/ 
|website=Innovative Genomics Institute 
|date=March 29, 2025
|access-date=March 30, 2025
}}</ref> and the [[Eli & Edythe Broad Center for Regeneration Medicine and Stem Cell Research]]. His work involves computational and [[synthetic biology]] approaches to study human disease, particularly through gene regulation and high-throughput screening techniques.<ref name="Bashyam2008" />

== Research contributions ==
McManus's research has encompassed the development of [[RNA interference]] technologies, including [[shRNA]] methodologies, and the application of deep sequencing in high-throughput gene perturbation screens. Notable contributions include:

* Developed RNA interference and [[shRNA]] technologies<ref name="Short hairpin RNAs shRNAs induce"/><ref name="A system for stable expression of s"/><ref name="Gene silencing using micro-RNA desi"/>
*Developed deep sequencing methods to analyze high-throughput gene perturbation screens, now a standard method in the field.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bassik |first1=Michael C. |last2=LeProust |first2=Emily M. |last3=Ebert |first3=Benjamin L. |last4=Rosenberg |first4=Samuel |last5=Ely |first5=Alex |last6=Holmes |first6=Andrew |last7=Jacobs |first7=H. == Awards and honors ==
In 2006, McManus received the WM Keck Award for establishing a Center for Noncoding RNAs.<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael McManus, PhD |url=https://cancer.ucsf.edu/people/mcmanus.michael |website=UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center |access-date=March 29, 2025}}</ref> In 2014, he received the NIH Transformative Research Award for his project on tracing cell lineages, focusing on developing high-throughput lineage tracing technologies.<ref name="NIHTransformativeResearch">{{Cite web 
|title=Funded Research - Transformative Research Award 
|url=https://commonfund.nih.gov/TRA/fundedresearch 
|website=NIH Common Fund 
|access-date=March 30, 2025
}}</ref> In 2019, he received the Robert J. Kleberg, Jr. and Helen C. Kleberg Award for his work on engineering cell-based mRNA delivery therapies.<ref name="KlebergFoundation">{{Cite web 
|title=The Robert J. Kleberg, Jr. and Helen C. Kleberg Foundation 
|url=https://www.klebergfoundation.org/ 
|website=Kleberg Foundation 
|access-date=March 30, 2025
}}</ref> Additional honors are detailed on his university's official website.<ref name="McManusLabAwards">{{Cite web 
|title=Awards and Honors 
|url=https://mcmanuslab.ucsf.edu/awards-and-honor 
|website=McManus Lab - UCSF 
|access-date=March 30, 2025
}}</ref>
